## Overview

This appendix documents every data source, cleaning operation, and merging step used to assemble the cluster-level analytic dataset for the micronutrient deficiency (MND) prediction pipeline. The pipeline predicts biomarker-defined deficiency in four micronutrients (vitamin A, iron, folate, vitamin B₁₂; zinc for Malawi only), in two populations (children 6–59 months, women 15–49 years), across four country-specific micronutrient surveys.

The primary modelling framing is **proxy-only**: the predictor matrix excludes all variables derived from the same biomarker survey as the outcome (any column with the `gw_` prefix is dropped at fitting time). A sensitivity model that retains `gw_` survey-derived variables is reported as a supplementary analysis.

All predictor sources are organised into eleven **domain prefixes** that define both the column-naming convention in the merged dataset and the unit of analysis for domain-level variable importance / domain ablation:

| Prefix | Domain | Conceptual content |
|---|---|---|
| `gw_` | Ground-truth Wide | Variables derived from the biomarker survey itself (excluded from primary models) |
| `dhs<year>_` | DHS | Demographic and Health Surveys, model-based admin1 and admin2 indicators |
| `mics_` | MICS | UNICEF Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys, admin1 region summaries |
| `ihme_` | IHME GBD geospatial | Modeled prevalence/incidence at admin1 and admin2 from IHME's geospatial releases |
| `lsms_` | LSMS | World Bank Living Standards Measurement Study (Integrated Surveys on Agriculture) — Ghana only |
| `MAP_` | Malaria Atlas | Malaria epidemiology, malaria interventions, blood-disorder gene frequencies |
| `wfp_` | WFP food prices | Commodity prices at nearest market, filtered to clusters ≤100 km from a market |
| `flunet_` | FluNet | WHO global influenza surveillance — Ghana only |
| `gee_` | Google Earth Engine | Satellite-derived climate, vegetation, soil, demographic, infrastructure rasters (cluster-buffer + admin2 zonal + survey-year-aligned + derived seasonality and YoY features) |
| `fsec_` | Food security | Cadre Harmonisé (West Africa) / HFID & FEWS NET IPC food security phase classifications |
| `soil_` | SoilGrids/ISRIC | Soil pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, clay, sand, silt, CEC at 0–5 cm, zonal-mean per Admin-2 |

Domain prefixes are configured in `R/config.R` per country and consumed by `R/sl_fitting.R`, `R/domain_ablation.R`, and `R/single_var_ablation.R` for variable selection and importance analysis.

## Outcome data

### Biomarker surveys

| Country | Survey | Fieldwork | N children | N women | Outcomes (biomarkers) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Gambia** | Gambia National Micronutrient Survey (GMNS) 2018 | 13 Mar – 4 May 2018 | ~1,600 | ~1,800 | RBP-Thurnham (vit A), ferritin-Brinda (iron) |
| **Ghana** | Ghana Micronutrient Survey (GMS) 2017 | 27 Apr – 9 Jun 2017 | 1,165 | ~992 | RBP-Thurnham (vit A), ferritin-Brinda (iron), serum folate, serum B₁₂ |
| **Sierra Leone** | Sierra Leone Micronutrient Survey (SLMS) 2013 | 11 Nov – 2 Dec 2013 | 532 | 945 | RBP (vit A), ferritin (iron), folate, B₁₂ |
| **Malawi** | Malawi Micronutrient Survey (MNS) 2015–16 | 8 Dec 2015 – 16 Feb 2016 | ~1,500 | ~700 | RBP (vit A), serum ferritin (iron), folate, B₁₂, serum zinc |

Each country's survey provides cluster-level GPS coordinates, a survey weight, primary sampling unit, stratum, and biomarker values. Population filtering (children vs women) uses a country-specific `child_flag` column documented in `R/config.R`.

### Outcome definitions

Each outcome (population × micronutrient combination) has both a continuous biomarker value and a binary deficiency indicator computed with WHO / Brinda / Thurnham thresholds:

- **Vitamin A**: serum RBP < 0.70 µmol/L (children & women)
- **Iron — children**: ferritin < 12 µg/L (inflammation-adjusted)
- **Iron — women**: ferritin < 15 µg/L (inflammation-adjusted)
- **Folate**: serum folate < 10 nmol/L (Ghana, SL); < 3 ng/mL in Malawi (study convention)
- **B₁₂**: serum B₁₂ < 148 pmol/L
- **Zinc** (Malawi only): serum zinc < 65 µg/dL (children, IZiNCG) / < 66 µg/dL (women, IZiNCG)

#### Inflammation adjustment per country (ferritin)

Acute / chronic inflammation elevates serum ferritin and can mask iron deficiency. The pipeline uses inflammation-adjusted ferritin throughout, but the adjustment **method** differs by country based on what each survey's clean file provides:

| Country | Continuous (modeling target) | Binary | Adjustment method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gambia | `gw_LogFerAdj` | `gw_cIDA_Brinda` / `gw_wIDA_Brinda` | Brinda |
| Ghana  | `gw_cLogFerrAdjThurn` / `gw_wLogFerrAdjThurn` (derived in Stage 1 from `gw_cFerrAdjThurn` / `gw_wFerrAdjThurn`) | `gw_cIDAdjThurn` / `gw_wIDA_Thurn` | Thurnham |
| Sierra Leone | `gw_cFerrAdj` / `gw_wFerAdjBR1` | `gw_cIDA` / `gw_wIDA` | Mixed (raw "Adj" suffix; Brinda for women) |
| Malawi | `sf_reg` (raw) | `iron_def` | None (raw biomarker) |

Both Brinda and Thurnham apply CRP/AGP-based corrections; results are highly correlated. The 2026-05-13 update switched Ghana from un-adjusted continuous ferritin (`gw_cLogFerr`) to Thurnham-adjusted (`gw_cLogFerrAdjThurn` derived in `1_GW_Ghana_data_clean.R`) to align with Ghana's already-adjusted binary outcome and reduce cross-country bias. The remaining Brinda-vs-Thurnham mismatch is documented as a limitation; a full BRINDA-package re-derivation for all four countries is recommended for the published manuscript.

Outcome definitions are encoded in `R/config.R::get_country_configs()` per country. Continuous biomarkers are log-transformed; the conformal regression target is fitted on the log scale.

## Predictor domains

### Domain 1 — Survey biomarker matrix (`gw_`, excluded from primary models)

Each survey's own data table provides ~330–600 variables prefixed `gw_`. These include the raw biomarkers (which would constitute outcome leakage), but also survey-design covariates (cluster, stratum), household-level variables (water source, mother's education), individual-level variables (age, sex), and derived indices. **None of the `gw_` variables enter the primary model**; an exclusion pattern in `R/config.R` (`gw_exclude_patterns`) ensures no covariate name matching `{RBP, VAD, LogFer, IDA, Brinda, Thurn, Folate, B12, Zinc, ...}` survives even in the sensitivity analysis.

### Domain 2 — DHS (`dhs<year>_`)

Two separate join paths:

- **Admin-1 direct estimates** (`R/data_prep.R::load_dhs_admin1()`): direct survey-weighted estimates of ~20 DHS indicators (mortality, anthropometry, anemia prevalence, fertility, child-feeding indicators, WASH access, women's education) at admin-1 region level, prefixed `dhs<year>_`. Joined to survey data on a country-specific Admin1 column (sometimes `Admin1_old` to match DHS legacy naming).
- **Admin-2 smoothed estimates** (`R/data_prep.R::load_dhs_admin2()`): same indicator set re-estimated at admin-2 via Fay–Herriot BYM2 spatial smoothing (surveyPrev), suffixed `_adm2`. Joined on Admin2 with fuzzy name matching (`R/food_security.R::build_name_lookup()`) since GADM admin-2 names may differ slightly from DHS region names.

DHS round per country:
- Gambia → DHS 2019 (closest available; no 2018 round)
- Ghana → DHS 2014 (TODO: upgrade to DHS 2017 once admin-2 aggregation is pre-computed; see `src/DHS/DHS_admin2_aggregation.R`)
- Sierra Leone → DHS 2013
- Malawi → DHS 2015

### Domain 3 — MICS (`mics_`)

UNICEF MICS region-level summaries from `data/MICS/mics_<country>_<year>_region_summary.csv`. Wide table keyed on `mics_region`, joined to survey data on Admin1. Contents are UNICEF-published region-level indicators (child mortality, stunting, vaccination, WASH, women's literacy, etc.). MICS is available for **Gambia (2018)** and **Ghana (2017)** only; not available for SL/Malawi in the current pipeline.

### Domain 4 — IHME GBD geospatial estimates (`ihme_`)

IHME releases geospatial models (~5 km gridded posterior mean prevalence) for several morbidity / nutrition / coverage indicators in LMICs. We use the published Admin-2 and Admin-1 aggregates of these models, organised into 13 indicator families:

| Folder | Indicator family | Years |
|---|---|---|
| `data/IHME/Anemia/` | All / mild / moderate / severe anemia prevalence | 2000–2019 |
| `data/IHME/CGF/` | Stunting / wasting / underweight prevalence | 2000–2017 |
| `data/IHME/DBM/` | Overweight / wasting prevalence (overweight is unique to DBM) | 2000–2017 |
| `data/IHME/EBF/` | Exclusive breastfeeding prevalence | 2000–2019 |
| `data/IHME/HIV/` | HIV prevalence + people-living-with-HIV counts | 2000–2018 |
| `data/IHME/LF/` | Lymphatic filariasis prevalence + counts | 2000–2018 |
| `data/IHME/Malaria/` | Pf/Pv incidence, prevalence, mortality | 2000–2019 |
| `data/IHME/u5 diarrhea/` | Under-5 diarrhea incidence / mortality / prevalence | 2000–2019 |
| `data/IHME/u5 mort/` | Under-5 mortality, infant mortality, neonatal mortality | 2000–2017 |
| `data/IHME/mcv1/` | Measles-containing vaccine 1 coverage | 2000–2019 |
| `data/IHME/oral rehydration/` | ORS / ORT / RHF coverage | 2000–2017 |
| `data/IHME/WASH access/` | Improved water/sanitation, piped, OD, etc. | 2000–2017 |
| `data/IHME/education/` | Mean years attainment, no-primary/primary/secondary proportion (M/F 15–49, 20–24) | 2000–2017 |

#### Admin-2 ingest (`src/<Country>/IHME_clean.R`)

Each country has a pre-merged rollup file (`data/IHME/IHME_<Country>_data.{csv,dta}`) containing all 13 indicator families at admin-2 in long format with columns `adm0_name, adm1_name, adm2_name, year, age_group_name, sex, measure, metric, mean, source`. The country clean script:

1. Filters to country and survey year.
2. Drops two duplicate sources (deduplication is at the source × measure level):
   - **`africa hiv prevalence geospatial estimates 2000-2017`** dropped entirely (superseded by the newer `sub-saharan africa hiv prevalence geospatial estimates 2000-2018` which has identical measures).
   - **`lmic dbm geospatial estimates 2000-2017` × `Wasting prevalence`** dropped (covered by CGF wasting); DBM overweight prevalence is retained because no other source provides it.
3. Renames a handful of ambiguous `measure` strings (e.g. "Incidence" → "malaria incidence") for unique-column identification.
4. Pivots wide on (`age_group_name`, `age_group_id`, `sex`, `measure`, `metric`), keyed on `adm2_name`, with all columns prefixed `ihme_`.

#### Admin-1 ingest (`src/IHME/build_ihme_admin1.R`, new in 2026-05)

The country rollup file contains only admin-2 rows. Admin-1 estimates are pulled directly from the per-indicator subfolders under `data/IHME/<family>/Data [CSV]/IHME_*_ADMIN_1_*.CSV` (also handles `_AD1_` / `_ADM1_` variants for legacy file-naming families). For each country × survey year:

1. Discover all admin-1 CSVs across the 13 indicator folders.
2. Skip the DBM wasting admin-1 file (duplicates CGF wasting).
3. For each file: filter to the country and the closest available year to survey year, build a long row per admin-1 unit × stratifier (age / sex / measure / metric), pivot wide on `adm1_name`, prefix `ihme_adm1_`.
4. Write `data/IHME/<country>_<year>_merged_IHME_admin1_data.csv`.

#### Merging into the survey data

The country merge scripts (`src/<Country>/2_GW_<Country>_data_merge.R`) load both CSVs and left-join on Admin1 (Jaro-Winkler fuzzy match, threshold 0.85) and Admin2 (`stringdist::stringdistmatrix` with jw/cosine/jaccard methods, threshold 0.90). Districts that don't match leave `NA` in the IHME columns (no imputation).

### Domain 5 — LSMS (`lsms_`)

World Bank LSMS-ISA household-survey aggregates. **Wired only for Ghana** at present; the Gambia merge script (`src/Gambia/2_GW_Gambia_data_merge.R:532`) has a stub block (`# TO ADD`) with intended-shape code commented out. LSMS is not available for Sierra Leone or Malawi.

### Domain 6 — Malaria Atlas (`MAP_`)

GeoTIFF rasters from the Malaria Atlas Project (MAP, `malariaAtlas` R package, dataset IDs from `data/Malaria Atlas/GHA_raster_list.xlsx`). Rasters live in `data/Malaria Atlas/<Country>/` and are read in the merge scripts via a hard-coded vector of filenames. `terra::extract()` with `method="bilinear"` extracts the cluster-GPS value, columns renamed `MAP_*`:

- **Malaria epidemiology (10 layers)**: 2022.06 + 2024.06 releases of *P. falciparum* and *P. vivax* incidence (count, rate), parasite rate, mortality (count, rate); plus 2022.02 *Pf* reproductive number.
- **Malaria interventions (10 layers)**: 2021.06 + 2024.06 ITN access, ITN use, ITN use rate, IRS coverage, antimalarial effective treatment.
- **Blood disorders (4 layers, added 2026-05)**: HbS allele frequency, HbC allele frequency, G6PDd allele frequency, Duffy negativity phenotype frequency. These control for hemolytic anemia and HbS/HbC confounders of ferritin-based iron status assessments. `ensure_map_blood_disorders()` in each merge script auto-downloads missing files via `malariaAtlas::getRaster()`.

### Domain 7 — GEE rasters (`gee_`)

Two complementary extractions:

#### Cluster-buffer summaries (existing)

Pre-extracted multi-radius buffer summaries (10 / 25 / 50 km circles around each cluster GPS) for 9 raster families, joined on cluster ID:

| Family | Source | Cadence in CSV |
|---|---|---|
| `trmm_<month>_<scale>` | TRMM precipitation | Monthly (Jan–Dec) × 3 buffer scales |
| `ndvi_<month>_<scale>` | NDVI | Monthly × 3 scales |
| `temp_<month>_<scale>` | Land-surface temperature | Monthly × 3 scales |
| `tpp_<def>_<scale>` / `fpp_<def>_<scale>` | Population density at 1 km / 500 m / cropland | Single value × 3 scales |
| `built_surface_<scale>` / `built_surface_nres_<scale>` | GHSL Built-Up | Single × 3 scales |
| `smod_<scale>` | GHSL Settlement Model | Single × 3 scales |
| `ghm_<scale>` | Global Human Modification | Single × 3 scales |
| `grassland_<scale>` | GPW grasslands | Single × 3 scales |

Buffer CSVs (`data/GEE/<country><year>_buffers_01.08.2026.csv`) were produced by an external Earth Engine export script (see `data/GEE/GEE Source Code for raster files.docx`).

#### Admin-2 zonal means (new in 2026-05, `src/GEE/extract_gee_admin2.R`, `scripts/build_gee_admin2.R`)

Per-Admin-2 polygon zonal means for **every** raster in `data/<Country>_GEE_rasters/` plus the four shared global rasters in `data/GEE/`. Implementation details:

1. **Year selection per family.** For each raster family, pick the single file whose embedded year matches the country's survey year (Gambia 2018, Ghana 2017, SL 2013, Malawi targets 2016 with 2015 fallback). If a family has only no-year files (e.g. iSDA `Soil*_<Country>.tif`), it's used as-is. If a year-specific file exists, the no-year file is dropped to avoid duplicate columns.
2. **Temporal aggregation.** Multi-band rasters whose bands are temporal sub-divisions of one year (detected via `terra::time()` metadata, filename keywords *Monthly* / *Daily* / *8days* / *Hourly*, or band count > 31 outside a known variable-stack family) are collapsed to one column per polygon: the mean across bands = **annual mean for the survey year**.
3. **Variable-stack handling.** Multi-band rasters where bands represent different variables (TerraClimate, LandCoverLayers/Type, GPW_Demographic age bins, FLDAS Annual_Mean, WAPOR, Productivity, ESA_WorldCereal) keep one column per band, with the band name (when present in `names(r)`) as the column suffix.
4. **CRS handling.** Polygons are reprojected to the raster's CRS before extraction (`terra::extract` with `weights = TRUE` for partial-pixel coverage at polygon edges).
5. **Output.** One CSV per country: `data/GEE/<Country>_<year>_admin2_gee.csv`, joined to the survey on `Admin2` in each merge script. All columns prefixed `gee_a2_` so they enter the GEE domain.

Raster families processed (after year selection):

- **Soil chemistry (11 families × 4 bands each = 44 columns)**: SoilZinc, SoilIron, SoilCalcium, SoilMagnesium, SoilPhosphorus, SoilPotassium, SoilSulfur, SoilNitrogen, SoilTotalCarbon, SoilCEC, SoilAluminium — from iSDAsoil
- **Climate**: TerraClimate (14-variable annual stack), TRMM (annual precipitation), FLDAS annual mean + monthly (collapsed), AerosolOptical, Atmosphere (daily, collapsed), LST_Night Annual_Mean + Monthly (collapsed)
- **Vegetation / agriculture**: NDVI (annual), NDVI Mean Anomaly, DailyEVI (collapsed), LAI8days (collapsed), Productivity, WAPOR, ESA_WorldCereal (cropland class layers), GPW_Grasslands
- **Settlement / human modification**: GHSBUILTS, GHSPOP, GHSL_SMOD, GlobalHumanModification, CCNL, WSF, PopDensity (annual), Elevation
- **Access / infrastructure**: Accessibility (travel time to healthcare)
- **Demographic**: GPW_Demographic (age-bin stack)
- **Land cover**: LandCoverLayers, LandCoverType
- **Livestock** (global): GLW4 GLEAM3 (FAO Global Livestock of the World, livestock density)

### Domain 8 — WFP food prices (`wfp_`)

World Food Programme food-price database (`data/food_price/wfp_food_prices_<iso>.csv`). For each cluster, the merge script finds the nearest WFP market by haversine distance (`sf::st_distance`), pivots commodity-level mean prices for the survey year into a wide table, and joins as `wfp_<commodity>` columns. The cluster also carries the `nearest_market_id` for downstream interpretation.

### Domain 9 — FluNet (`flunet_`)

WHO Global Influenza Surveillance (FluNet) — weekly virological surveillance counts at the country level. Joined where available (Ghana only in current pipeline). Provides time-lagged influenza positivity rates as a marker of seasonal respiratory disease pressure.

### Domain 10 — Food security (`fsec_`)

`R/food_security.R::merge_food_security()` is called near the end of each country's Stage 2 merge script (added 2026-05-13; previously defined but never invoked) and ingests two sources:

- **Cadre Harmonisé** (West African food security classification, December 2025 update): `data/CadreHarmonise/cadre_harmonise_caf_ipc_dec25.xlsx` + `wca_chipc_current_march2023.geojson`. Provides IPC-equivalent food-insecurity phase per admin region. Covers Gambia, Ghana, Sierra Leone; not Malawi.
- **HFID / FEWS NET IPC** (`data/HFID/hfid_hv1.csv`): same data structure, includes Malawi.

Columns include `fsec_ipc_phase_*`, `fsec_pop_phase_*` (population in each phase), and derived severity scores. The function tries Admin-2 merge first, falls back to Admin-1 if Admin-2 keys are unavailable.

### Domain 11 — SoilGrids/ISRIC (`soil_`)

`R/external_data.R::extract_soilgrids()` extracts seven properties at 0–5 cm depth (mean values) from the SoilGrids global VRT via `/vsicurl/` and computes zonal means per Admin-2 polygon:

- `soil_ph`, `soil_organic_carbon`, `soil_nitrogen`, `soil_clay`, `soil_sand`, `soil_silt`, `soil_cec`

Built by `scripts/build_soilgrids_admin2.R` per country into `data/SoilGrids/<Country>_soilgrids_admin2.csv`. Joined on `(Admin1, Admin2)` in each Stage 2 merge script (added 2026-05-13; previously defined but never invoked). This domain is **complementary** to the iSDAsoil micronutrient layers in the GEE folder — SoilGrids provides macro soil chemistry (pH, organic matter, particle size), while iSDA provides plant-available Fe / Zn / Ca / Mg / N / P / K / S etc. that flow in as `gee_a2_Soil*`.

## Derived feature engineering (2026-05-13)

Beyond raw predictor columns, the merge scripts derive several feature families. All are computed at cluster level (merging upstream domain-level data with row-level transformations) and inherit the parent domain's prefix.

### Seasonality summary features (from monthly GEE buffers)

The cluster-buffer GEE CSV contains 12 monthly columns per (family × scale) for `trmm_*`, `ndvi_*`, `temp_*` at 10/25/50 km — roughly 108 monthly columns per cluster. `src/GEE/seasonality_features.R::add_seasonality_features()` (called from each Stage 2 merge after the cluster-buffer join) derives five summary columns per (family, scale) pair:

| Suffix | Formula | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| `_annual_mean` | mean across 12 months | year-level baseline |
| `_seasonal_sd` | sd across months | absolute seasonal variability |
| `_seasonal_cv` | sd / |mean| | seasonality intensity (drought-vulnerability proxy) |
| `_seasonal_range` | max − min | absolute spread between wettest/greenest and driest/sparsest month |
| `_peak_month` | which.max | timing of peak (1=Jan, 12=Dec) — drives malaria seasonality, harvest timing |

These 5 dense features are more useful to the SuperLearner than 12 raw monthly columns. The monthly columns are retained alongside.

### Year-over-year (YoY) change features (from annual GEE rasters)

`scripts/build_gee_admin2.R` now selects two files per raster family when available: the survey-year file and the previous-year file. After extraction, a post-processing step computes per-Admin-2 YoY delta columns named `gee_a2_<family>_yoy_<curyr>_<prevyr>` (e.g. `gee_a2_NDVI_yoy_2018_2017`). YoY change captures *recent* trends (rapid urbanisation, drought emergence, vegetation recovery) which static-snapshot predictors miss.

### LSMS dietary-share proxies (Ghana)

The Ghana LSMS clean file is pre-aggregated to household level and does not include raw food-group consumption columns required for standard HDDS/MDD-W indices. As a substitute, the merge script derives three expenditure-share proxies (named `lsms_food_share_of_total`, `lsms_animal_source_share`, `lsms_fruit_share`) which correlate with dietary diversity. These map to biologically motivated micronutrient pathways: animal-source food share for iron/B₁₂, fruit share for vitamin A/folate, food expenditure share as a proxy for poverty (Engel's law).

### LSMS / WFP / nearest-market distance quality filter

WFP commodity prices are joined by `nearest_market_id` regardless of distance. Stage 2 now sets all `wfp_*` columns to `NA` for clusters whose nearest market is **>100 km** away (configurable `WFP_MAX_DIST_KM` constant per script). This prevents distant-market noise from polluting the predictor matrix in remote clusters.

## Pipeline architecture and helper files

### Stage 1 cleaning scripts

Each country has a Stage 1 script that reads raw biomarker survey .dta files and emits a per-country cleaned RDS. Conventions:

| Country | Stage 1 script | Output path |
|---|---|---|
| Gambia | `src/Gambia/1_GW_Gambia_data_clean.R` | `data/IPD/Gambia/Gambia_GMS_cleaned.rds` |
| Ghana | `src/Ghana/1_GW_Ghana_data_clean.R` | `data/IPD/Ghana/Ghana_GMS_cleaned.rds` |
| Sierra Leone | `src/SierraLeone/1_GW_SierraLeone_data_clean.R` | `data/IPD/Sierra Leone/SierraLeone_GMS_cleaned.rds` |
| **Malawi** | `src/malawi/1_DHS_mn_data.R` (legacy naming) | `data/IPD/Malawi/clean_malawi_mn_data.RDS` |

The Malawi script's name is a legacy artifact ("DHS" refers to the older Demographic-and-Health-Survey-style code generation; the script actually processes the Malawi Micronutrient Survey). A standardisation rename (to `1_GW_Malawi_data_clean.R`) is planned but defers the file move.

The Ghana Stage 1 script now also (2026-05-13):
- Guards `parse_date_time()` against silent NA fallback with a 95% parse-success assertion.
- Derives `gw_cLogFerrAdjThurn` and `gw_wLogFerrAdjThurn` from `gw_cFerrAdjThurn` / `gw_wFerrAdjThurn` for outcome modeling (see ferritin discussion above).

### Helper modules sourced by Stage 1 + Stage 2

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/0-functions.R` | Bench of small utilities: `fuzzy_match_admin2()`, `clean_DHS()`, `getDHSdata()`, `makeVlist()`, `evaluate_sl_performance()`. Sourced at the top of every Stage 1 script. |
| `src/0-SL-setup.R` | SuperLearner / `sl3` configuration. Sourced where the modelling stack is set up (currently in `R/sl_fitting.R`, not the merge scripts). |
| `src/DHS/DHS_functions.R` | DHS-specific helpers used by `getDHSdata()`. |
| `src/DHS/DHS_variable_recode.R` | DHS variable name harmonisation across survey years. |
| `R/data_prep.R` | Higher-level wrappers: `load_gadm_cached()`, `load_dhs_admin1()`, `load_dhs_admin2()`, `build_outcome_dataset()` (domain assignment). |
| `R/external_data.R` | Generic admin-2 zonal-mean extractors for SoilGrids, CHIRPS, WorldPop, NTL, MAP. `extract_soilgrids()` is wired into the merge pipeline (2026-05-13); the others remain dormant — see "Dormant helpers" note below. |
| `R/merge_external.R` | Join utilities (e.g. `merge_by_admin()`) with duplicate-key guards. |
| `R/food_security.R` | `merge_food_security()` for CH + HFID — wired into all four Stage 2 scripts (2026-05-13). |
| `src/IHME/build_ihme_admin1.R` | IHME admin-1 wide table builder and merge helper with fuzzy admin matching. |
| `src/GEE/extract_gee_admin2.R` | GEE admin-2 zonal-mean extractor with temporal-aggregation heuristics. |
| `src/GEE/seasonality_features.R` | Derives seasonality summary features from monthly buffer columns. |

### Dormant helpers

`R/external_data.R::extract_all_external()` is an orchestrator that wraps SoilGrids + CHIRPS + WorldPop + NTL + MAP extractions. SoilGrids is now invoked individually (via `scripts/build_soilgrids_admin2.R`); the other extractors in `extract_all_external()` overlap with the GEE buffer / admin-2 pipeline (CHIRPS ≈ TRMM, WorldPop ≈ GHSPOP, NTL ≈ CCNL) and remain dormant. A future cleanup should either wire the non-duplicate extracts (e.g. fine-resolution CHIRPS daily) or remove the dead code.

## Geographic harmonisation

### Polygons

All admin-1 / admin-2 polygons come from **GADM 4.1** via `R/data_prep.R::load_gadm_cached()`, cached in `data/gadm/`. Standardised column names are `Admin1` (= GADM `NAME_1`) and `Admin2` (= `NAME_2`).

### Cluster → admin assignment

Survey clusters are point-located (lat/lon). Admin1 and Admin2 are assigned by `sf::st_join(d_sf, poly.adm, join = st_within)` in each country's merge script. Clusters that fall outside any polygon (rare; coastal-shift) are dropped with a warning.

### Fuzzy Admin name matching for merges

GADM names often differ from DHS / IHME / MICS region names by small spelling/diacritic variants. The merge scripts use one of two approaches:

1. **`fuzzy_match_admin2()`** (in each country merge script): Jaro-Winkler + cosine + Jaccard via `stringdist::stringdistmatrix`, ensemble-best match, similarity threshold 0.90 for IHME admin-2.
2. **`build_name_lookup()`** (in `R/food_security.R`): single-method Jaro-Winkler with threshold 0.80 for DHS admin-2 and Cadre Harmonisé.

For admin-1 the merge uses an admin1-equivalent helper (`merge_ihme_admin1()`) with Jaro-Winkler threshold 0.85. Each merge logs the number of matched / unmatched units; districts that don't match are left as `NA` rather than coerced.

### Country-specific admin-1 legacy mapping

Some surveys/external sources use an older admin-1 partition (e.g. Gambia's "Maccarthy Island" → Kuntaur / Janjanbureh split, Ghana's pre-2018 ten-region geography). The merge scripts maintain an `Admin1_old` column derived from a `case_when()` lookup, used to join DHS / MICS legacy-named tables.

---

## Temporal alignment

The pipeline aligns each external predictor to the survey year as closely as the source allows. Conventions:

| Source | Alignment rule |
|---|---|
| DHS | Closest available DHS round to survey year (Gambia DHS 2019 ↔ MNS 2018; Ghana DHS 2014 ↔ GMS 2017, upgrade to 2017 pending; SL DHS 2013 ↔ SLMS 2013; Malawi DHS 2015 ↔ MNS 2015–16) |
| MICS | Closest published MICS round (Gambia 2018, Ghana 2017) |
| IHME admin2 (rollup) | Filtered to `year == survey_year` exactly |
| IHME admin1 (new) | Closest available year per indicator family (some families only run through 2017, 2018, or 2019) |
| MAP malaria/interventions | 2021.06 + 2024.06 releases (kept both for redundancy / temporal contrast) |
| MAP blood disorders | 2012.01 single release (genetic frequencies are time-invariant) |
| GEE cluster buffer | Buffer CSV pre-computed at survey year by external EE script |
| GEE admin-2 zonal | Per-family, nearest available year to survey year (Malawi targets 2016, falls back to 2015 for families that stop at 2015) |
| Multi-band annual rasters | Mean across bands within the chosen year = "average over survey year" |
| WFP food prices | Mean within survey year (`filter(year == survey_year)`) |
| Cadre Harmonisé / FEWS NET | Most recent published IPC classification |

---

## Cleaning conventions and exclusions

### `gw_` outcome-leakage exclusion patterns

`R/config.R` per country specifies `gw_exclude_patterns` — case-insensitive regex tokens that, if matched in a column name, drop the column from the `gw_` set before model fitting. Across countries the patterns are:

```
RBP, rbp, VAD, LogFer, logfer, IDA, Brinda, Thurn,
Ferr, ferr, FeD, LogRBP,
Folate, folate, Fol, B12, b12, Zinc, zinc
```

The `gw_` domain is also dropped entirely from primary models — these patterns are a defence-in-depth check for the supplementary sensitivity model that retains `gw_`.

### Dropping high-cardinality categoricals

`check_categorical_levels(df, max_levels = 100)` drops any factor/character column with > 100 levels (typically free-text fields, dates parsed as strings, cluster IDs that were not converted to integer).

### Geometry / temporal columns

All `sf` geometry columns are dropped (`st_drop_geometry`) before saving the analytic table; all `POSIXct` / `POSIXt` columns are dropped.

### Final analytic table

Each country's merge script writes `data/IPD/<Country>/<Country>_merged_dataset.rds` and a corresponding `metadata/<country>_variable_categories.rds` recording which columns belong to which domain (for downstream variable importance and domain ablation).

The `soil_` domain shows 100% NA for Gambia/SL/Malawi because the ISRIC SoilGrids VRT download failed for those countries on the most recent run (network/server flakiness). The infrastructure is in place; re-running `scripts/build_soilgrids_admin2.R` will populate the domain when ISRIC's file server is responsive. Ghana succeeded on first attempt and has 98% non-NA soil data.

The `fsec_` 75–83% NA rates reflect that food-security IPC classifications are only published for specific admin units (and only some have current-period data); the remaining clusters get NA. This is informative missingness, not a defect.

## Domain definitions used in variable importance

The variable importance and domain ablation analyses operate on the ten domains defined in `R/config.R::get_country_configs()$<country>$domains`. Each domain entry has a `prefix` string; the column-selection logic in `R/domain_ablation.R::domain_columns()` is essentially `grep(prefix, colnames(X), fixed = TRUE)`. Operationally:

- **Domain ablation** (`R/domain_ablation.R`): fits the full SuperLearner, then for each domain in turn re-evaluates predictions using a leave-one-domain-out predictor matrix (drops all columns matching that domain's prefix). The ΔAUC / ΔRMSE relative to the full model is the domain's importance score. Reported per outcome × country.
- **Single-variable importance** (`R/single_var_ablation.R`): permutation-based per-column drop in AUC, top-30 retained per outcome.
- **SHAP explanations** (`R/shap_explanations.R`): extracts xgboost SHAP attributions for the best xgboost candidate in the SL stack, aggregates to admin-2 level for the dashboard's per-district top-predictor display.

### Prefix matching rules per domain

| Domain | Prefix(es) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GW | `gw_` | Excluded from primary models; only enters supplementary sensitivity |
| DHS | `dhs<year>_` (year is country-specific) | Includes both admin-1 direct and admin-2 BYM2-smoothed columns; admin-2 columns have a `_adm2` suffix on top of the prefix |
| MICS | `mics_` | Admin-1 region summaries |
| IHME | `ihme_` (also catches `ihme_adm1_`) | Admin-1 and admin-2 both fall under this single domain |
| LSMS | `lsms_` | Ghana only |
| MAP | `MAP_` | Malaria epidemiology + interventions + blood disorders (case-sensitive: capital `MAP_`) |
| WFP | `wfp_`, plus `nearest_market_id` | Food prices |
| FLUNET | `flunet_` | Ghana only |
| GEE | `gee_` (also catches `gee_a2_`) | Cluster buffer + admin-2 zonal both fall under this single domain |
| FSEC | `fsec_` | Food security phase |

Because both IHME variants (`ihme_` admin-2 and `ihme_adm1_` admin-1) share the `ihme_` prefix, domain ablation drops both together — appropriate, since they share an underlying source. Similarly both GEE variants share the `gee_` prefix and are ablated jointly. A future enhancement could ablate the variants separately (`ihme_` vs `ihme_adm1_`; `gee_` cluster-buffer vs `gee_a2_` admin-2 zonal) by adjusting `domain_columns()`.

## Data quality and coverage gaps

| Country | Notable gaps | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| Gambia 2018 | No LSMS (stub at `src/Gambia/2_GW_Gambia_data_merge.R:532`); IHME indicators stopping at 2017 are missing (CGF, U5M, ORT, education, u5 diarrhea) — admin-1 IHME column count is lower for Gambia (58 vs 117 for the others) | Coverage of household-level food access proxies is weak; some IHME nutrition indicators absent |
| Ghana 2017 | DHS 2014 used (3-year gap before survey); LightGBM / neural net learners disabled due to silent failures (`R/mlr3_fitting.R:92`) | DHS misalignment is small but worth a sensitivity check once DHS 2017 admin-2 is run |
| Sierra Leone 2013 | No MICS, LSMS, FluNet, WFP wired; sometimes errors during cluster-CV refit (data-prep audit recommended for `outcome_data` target) | Domain matrix is smaller than for Gambia / Ghana; transportability claim is weaker |
| Malawi 2015–16 | No MICS, LSMS, FluNet; GEE rasters mostly end at 2015 (target 2016 falls back to 2015 for several families) | Predictor matrix uses 2015 vintage data; survey was conducted mostly in Jan–Feb 2016 — minor temporal misalignment |

## Reproducibility checklist

The complete data assembly for one country is:

```bash
# 1. Pre-compute IHME admin-2 wide (deduplication applied)
Rscript src/<Country>/<country>_IHME_clean.R
# (the same script chains a call to build_ihme_admin1() and writes
#  data/IHME/<country>_<year>_merged_IHME_admin1_data.csv)

# 2. Pre-compute GEE admin-2 zonal means
Rscript scripts/build_gee_admin2.R <Country>

# 3. Assemble the analytic table
Rscript src/<Country>/2_GW_<Country>_data_merge.R
# (auto-downloads MAP blood-disorder rasters if missing,
#  joins cluster-buffer GEE, admin-2 GEE, MAP rasters, DHS,
#  MICS, IHME, WFP, FluNet, FSEC, Soil)

# Output: data/IPD/<Country>/<Country>_merged_dataset.rds
#         metadata/<country>_variable_categories.rds
```

The targets pipeline (`_targets.R`) reads only the per-country merged RDS — it does not re-run any of the steps above. To refresh predictors after upstream changes:

```r
targets::tar_invalidate(names = matches("^outcome_data_"))
targets::tar_make_future(workers = 4)
```
